2026-11-05.headline: Purview retention splits Copilot coverage; auto-labeling capped at 500,000 files daily
2026-11-05.overview: Two administrator-relevant updates stand out. Beginning January 15, 2027, the “Teams chats and Copilot interactions” retention location will cover Teams content only, while updated Information Protection guidance defines 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant per day as an absolute aggregate ceiling across all auto-labeling policies, not a guaranteed processing rate. Related Purview pages now reflect the same ceiling.
2026-11-05.adminImpact: Administrators needing Microsoft 365 Copilot interaction retention should create a separate retention policy using the “Microsoft Copilot Experiences” location. For auto-labeling, plan against one tenant-wide limit across all policies and expect actual throughput to be lower than 500,000 files per day; Teams retention behavior remains unchanged.

keyChanges.title: Teams and Copilot retention coverage separates on January 15, 2027
keyChanges.detail: Policies using “Teams chats and Copilot interactions” will apply only to Teams content beginning January 15, 2027. They will no longer retain or delete Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions, including previously retained interactions. Use the separate “Microsoft Copilot Experiences” location when Copilot retention is required.

keyChanges.title: Auto-labeling throughput is an aggregate tenant ceiling, not a rate
keyChanges.detail: The limit for automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files is stated as an absolute maximum of 500,000 files per tenant per day across all auto-labeling policies. Actual throughput may be lower, so administrators should assess volume across the tenant rather than treating the figure as an expected daily processing rate.

2026-11-06.headline: DLP adds a control to exclude external emails from Copilot grounding
2026-11-06.overview: A new admin-configurable Purview DLP control is described for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat. It restricts processing of email from external or untrusted domains while preserving internal data use. The period also adds more precise auto-label simulation troubleshooting and a new audit activity for gateway datasource status tests.
2026-11-06.adminImpact: Administrators can assess the DLP control against their Copilot data-handling requirements and track the stated public preview and general availability timing. For auto-label simulations, they can distinguish failed jobs from requests that never started, interpret partial results, preserve useful results before restarting, and review workload details before enabling a policy. Audit teams can use the new activity name to identify tenant administrator connection status tests.

keyChanges.title: DLP can exclude external email from Copilot grounding
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center item describes a new admin-configurable DLP control for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat. It excludes email from external or untrusted domains from Copilot grounding while maintaining internal data use; the item lists public preview in June 2026 and general availability in June 2027.

keyChanges.title: Auto-label guidance adds failure and partial-result handling
keyChanges.detail: The Auto Label Simulation Results article adds the “Simulation failed” status, distinguishes failed jobs from requests that could not start, explains partial workload counts, and provides guidance for reviewing or restarting simulations. Administrators are told to preserve useful results before restarting and review workload details before enabling a policy.

keyChanges.title: Audit references gateway datasource status test activity
keyChanges.detail: The Audit Log Activities reference now includes GetGatewayClusterDatasourceStatusAsAdmin for tenant administrator connection status tests, giving administrators the activity name needed to identify those tests in audit records.

keyChanges.title: Sensitivity-label guidance links simulation failure details
keyChanges.detail: Apply Sensitivity Label Automatically now links to guidance for simulation failure messages and results marked “(partial)”. The change helps administrators find the relevant troubleshooting guidance when simulations fail or produce partial results.

2026-11-07.headline: Audit activity reference adds Power BI MCP semantic-model event names
2026-11-07.overview: The Audit Log Activities documentation now lists events for Power BI MCP tools that modify semantic models and read semantic model metadata.
2026-11-07.adminImpact: Administrators can use these activity names when reviewing or interpreting audit logs. No action is required.

keyChanges.title: Power BI MCP activity coverage documented
keyChanges.detail: The activity reference adds event names for MCP tools modifying semantic models and reading semantic model metadata.

2026-11-09.headline: Purview retires four DSPM partner integrations December 7 as permissions auditing expands
2026-11-09.overview: Microsoft Purview will retire its Varonis, BigID, Cyera, and OneTrust DSPM integrations for non-Microsoft data sources on December 7, 2026. Separately, Purview is adding two audit operations for role-based access control, with worldwide rollout scheduled from late September through mid-November 2026.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: Administrators using the affected DSPM integrations should review dependencies before December 7; those integrations will stop ingesting and displaying data, while other DSPM capabilities remain unaffected. The permissions-audit improvements require no action but should provide more visibility for investigating access issues and monitoring compliance.

keyChanges.title: Four DSPM partner integrations will retire
keyChanges.detail: On December 7, 2026, Purview will retire the Varonis, BigID, Cyera, and OneTrust integrations for non-Microsoft data sources. They will no longer ingest or display data; other DSPM capabilities remain unaffected. Microsoft says no action is required, but administrators should review dependencies if they use these integrations.

keyChanges.title: RBAC permissions auditing gains two operations
keyChanges.detail: Purview is adding two new audit operations for role-based access control, improving transparency and troubleshooting for access issues. The enhancement is rolling out worldwide from late September through mid-November 2026 and requires no administrator action.

2026-11-10.headline: Purview DLP guidance names Cowork while DSPM documents Copilot label-inheritance limits
2026-11-10.overview: Cowork is the day's main thread: DLP guidance now calls the location “Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork,” adds Cowork to setup examples and supported experiences, and states that administrative-unit scoping applies to Cowork for Microsoft Copilot and Chat. DSPM guidance defines when new Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and PDF content can inherit source sensitivity labels and protection. Insider Risk also clarifies alternate-email associations, while two Message Center announcements outline a mid-2027 Endpoint DLP AI capability and a late-November 2026 Edge for Business setup change.
2026-11-10.adminImpact: Use the expanded Cowork wording when configuring DLP and verify administrative-unit-scoped coverage. For DSPM, set expectations using the documented 50 MB, label-availability, and user-defined-permission limits. Review alternate email addresses when Insider Risk activity appears under an unexpected profile. For planning, the Endpoint DLP skills require Security Copilot enabled; the Edge change adds Intune multi-admin approval and requires no policy migration.

keyChanges.title: DLP guidance now carries Cowork through location and scope references
keyChanges.detail: The DLP location is now named “Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork,” with Cowork added to setup guidance, examples, and supported experiences. The policy reference also states that administrative-unit scoping applies to Cowork for Microsoft Copilot and Chat.

keyChanges.title: DSPM documents sensitivity-label inheritance limits for Copilot content
keyChanges.detail: The guidance says new Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and PDF content can inherit the source item's sensitivity label and protection settings. User-defined-permission labels are unsupported, and labeling does not occur when the label is unavailable to the user or the file exceeds 50 MB.

keyChanges.title: Insider Risk explains alternate-email profile associations
keyChanges.detail: Insider Risk guidance now says alternate email addresses, including Microsoft Entra ID’s Other mail values, associate activity and historical activity with user profiles. Changing an address does not correct existing alerts or historical associations.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint DLP AI skills target mid-2027 with Security Copilot required
keyChanges.detail: A Message Center announcement describes AI-powered Policy Sync and Device Health skills for real-time visibility into policy deployment and synchronization issues, impacted devices, root causes, and remediation actions. The rollout is targeted for mid-2027 and requires Security Copilot enabled in the tenant.

keyChanges.title: Edge for Business DLP setup adds Intune multi-admin approval
keyChanges.detail: Purview DLP setup and activation for unmanaged apps in Edge for Business will gain clearer status, detailed errors, and task coordination between Purview and Intune administrators starting in late November 2026. No policy migration is needed.

2026-11-12.headline: Purview AI-readiness article adds action-oriented guidance and a four-part admin summary
2026-11-12.overview: The period brought one Purview update: the AI and Copilot guidance now presents recommendations more directly and adds a Summary section covering Purview’s role in understanding data, protecting sensitive information, investigating risks, and governing AI interactions.
2026-11-12.adminImpact: Admins preparing for AI apps and agents get clearer guidance for identifying and addressing data-protection gaps before those systems use organizational data.

keyChanges.title: AI-readiness guidance is more action-oriented
keyChanges.detail: The “Protect Sensitive Data To Get Ready For AI” article now uses action-oriented wording for its recommendations and adds a Summary section explaining how Purview can help admins understand data, protect sensitive information, investigate risks, and govern AI interactions.

2026-11-13.headline: Purview Unified Catalog guidance adds Fabric-consolidation notice and new-account restriction
2026-11-13.overview: The day was dominated by a retirement notice added across Unified Catalog and classic Microsoft Purview data governance guidance. Updated pages now state that these capabilities are being consolidated in Microsoft Fabric and that new accounts can no longer be created. The supplied guidance includes no migration deadline or specific migration procedure. A separate Communication Compliance update clarifies permissions for the Information Barriers SharePoint report.
2026-11-13.adminImpact: Administrators planning new governance deployments should account for the stated inability to create new Purview accounts and the consolidation into Microsoft Fabric. Existing environments should be assessed against the transition language on individual capability pages. For Information Barriers reporting, review whether SharePoint Embedded Administrator users should handle report execution and segment updates for user-owned containers.

keyChanges.title: Unified Catalog and classic governance pages add a retirement notice
keyChanges.detail: Updated Data Governance guidance now states that Unified Catalog and classic Purview data governance capabilities are being retired and consolidated in Microsoft Fabric, and that new accounts can no longer be created. The Enterprise Glossary page supplies no deadline or specific migration step.

keyChanges.title: Self-service policy guidance preserves existing capabilities during transition
keyChanges.detail: The updated Azure SQL Database self-service policies page repeats the retirement and new-account restriction but explicitly says existing capabilities remain available during the transition.

keyChanges.title: Information Barriers report guidance names the SharePoint Embedded Administrator role
keyChanges.detail: Users with the SharePoint Embedded Administrator role can run the Information Barriers SharePoint report and update segments for user-owned containers.

2026-11-14.headline: Adaptive scopes add active-only recipient and site-owner filtering in December 2026 preview
2026-11-14.overview: Two forward-looking rollouts carry the most administrator weight: adaptive scopes will shift to active-only recipient and site-owner evaluation by default, with a December 2026 preview and April 2027 general availability milestone; sensitivity labels for Microsoft Entra cloud security groups begin in mid-January 2027. The documentation updates add targeted operational guidance on Insider Risk group-removal delays, Outlook for Mac version requirements, and failed sensitivity-label audit operations.
2026-11-14.adminImpact: No immediate action is required for adaptive scopes. For Microsoft Entra security groups, administrators must plan for separate feature enablement and appropriate licensing, while recognizing that applied labels cannot currently be changed or removed. Insider Risk investigations should allow for processing delays and retained alerts or activity. Administrators supporting on-premises mailboxes should verify Outlook for Mac is version 16.112 or later, and use the revised audit operation names in searches and documentation.

keyChanges.title: Adaptive scopes default to active lifecycle objects
keyChanges.detail: Starting in the December 2026 preview, adaptive scopes will evaluate only active recipients and site owners by default, with options to include inactive or soft-deleted ones. Queries also gain ISO 8601 duration support, and general availability is scheduled for April 2027.

keyChanges.title: Sensitivity labels reach Microsoft Entra cloud security groups
keyChanges.detail: Beginning in mid-January 2027, sensitivity labels can be applied to Microsoft Entra cloud security groups for label-based governance and access policies. The feature must be enabled separately and requires appropriate licensing; labels cannot yet be changed or removed after application.

keyChanges.title: Insider Risk guidance details delayed group-removal effects
keyChanges.detail: Removing a user from an included security group may not immediately stop scoring or alerting. Activities can continue contributing to alerts until processing completes, collected activities remain stored through the activation window, and existing alerts are not automatically removed. Deleted accounts in two departing-user templates continue to be monitored for the rest of that window.

keyChanges.title: Outlook for Mac 16.112 supports labels for on-premises mailboxes
keyChanges.detail: The sensitivity-label guidance now specifies Outlook for Mac version 16.112 or later for on-premises mailbox support. Other Outlook clients still require Exchange Online, including when working with shared mailboxes.

keyChanges.title: Audit reference names failed sensitivity-label operations
keyChanges.detail: The documented operation names are now FileSensitivityLabelApplyFailed, FileSensitivityLabelChangeFailed, and FileSensitivityLabelRemoveFailed. Use these names when reviewing or documenting audit events for failed sensitivity-label actions.

2026-11-17.headline: Adaptive protection preview targets 120-day labels for high-risk-user deletions
2026-11-17.overview: Data Lifecycle Management’s Adaptive protection integration is the standout capability change: the public preview automatically applies retention labels to content deleted by elevated-risk users for 120 days, with general availability listed for early 2027. Other meaningful updates cover 2027 PST Import planning, a Teams Information Barriers procedure, Clipchamp label inheritance, and more precise auto-label reporting guidance.
2026-11-17.adminImpact: The main planning points are the 120-day retention behavior, Azure permissions and mailbox prerequisites for PST Import, and up to 24 hours for Information Barriers segment stamping after an Implicit-to-Explicit conversion. Admins reviewing Clipchamp should check the `EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles` tenant value. Reporting teams should treat Auto Label Insights activity as operations rather than distinct files and account for its refresh cadence and 30-day window.

keyChanges.title: Adaptive protection integrates with Data Lifecycle Management
keyChanges.detail: The public-preview integration automatically applies retention labels to content deleted by elevated-risk users for 120 days. Microsoft lists general availability for early 2027 and describes the setup as requiring minimal administrator configuration.

keyChanges.title: Azure PST Import is scheduled to begin in April 2027
keyChanges.detail: Admins will import PST files from Azure Blob Storage into Exchange Online mailboxes through PowerShell, with readiness analysis and import batching. The rollout requires specified Azure permissions and mailbox prerequisites, and imported data remains subject to existing retention and audit policies.

keyChanges.title: Information Barriers guidance documents Explicit-mode Teams conversion
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance explains how to change a Teams-connected Microsoft 365 group from Implicit to Explicit mode with PowerShell. It documents segment-based access and membership, up to 24 hours for segment stamping, and the restriction that site owners and SharePoint admins cannot manage segments on Explicit-mode Teams-connected sites. Owner moderated and Open modes cannot be transitioned.

keyChanges.title: Clipchamp labeling is tied to EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles
keyChanges.detail: The revised sensitivity-label guidance says `EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles` controls labeling for Clipchamp projects and whether exported MP4 files inherit the project’s label. Administrators should use the tenant’s current setting value when assessing the effect.

keyChanges.title: Auto Label Insights separates progress from recorded activity
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance distinguishes periodically refreshed labeling progress from recorded labeling activity over the last 30 days. Activity counts labeling operations rather than distinct files, and the documentation points admins to the newer full review experience for daily trends.

2026-11-18.headline: eDiscovery Graph guidance documents permanent Teams purges and GCC export-auth limits
2026-11-18.overview: The day’s most consequential changes are operational eDiscovery constraints: Teams-message purges are documented as permanent regardless of `purgeType`, must be requested separately from mailbox purges, and run first; a separate export guide adds a GCC restriction on app-based authentication. A forward-looking Message Center announcement schedules DLP and auto-labeling for connected non-Microsoft apps starting mid-March 2027, while other updates clarify Agent Builder Information Barriers behavior and SAP S/4HANA scan sizing.
2026-11-18.adminImpact: eDiscovery administrators need to separate mailbox and Teams purge requests, run Teams first, and treat `teamsMessages` deletion as irreversible. Graph script users should replace placeholders with the correct MicrosoftPurviewEDiscovery application ID and note that GCC administrators cannot use app-based authentication for export downloads. Agent Builder users should expect Information Barriers to hide restricted people in the picker, and SAP S/4HANA scan owners should review Self-hosted Integration Runtime sizing against the 128 GB RAM recommendation. The Message Center notice points to future connector-based DLP and auto-labeling coverage for apps such as Google Workspace, Box, and Salesforce, managed in Purview from mid-March 2027.

keyChanges.title: Teams-message purges are documented as permanent, with a required sequence
keyChanges.detail: The eDiscovery guidance states that `teamsMessages` purges permanently delete Teams messages regardless of `purgeType`. Mailbox and Teams purges require separate requests, with Teams first; the API returns `202 Accepted` and a status URL.

keyChanges.title: GCC cannot use app-based authentication for Graph eDiscovery export downloads
keyChanges.detail: The export guide adds the GCC limitation and clarifies the application IDs, scopes, and authentication parameters required by its scripts. Administrators should replace placeholder values with the correct MicrosoftPurviewEDiscovery application ID; GCC administrators cannot use app-based authentication for export downloads.

keyChanges.title: Purview schedules DLP and auto-labeling for connected non-Microsoft apps
keyChanges.detail: A Message Center notice says Purview will support DLP and auto-labeling for apps such as Google Workspace, Box, and Salesforce through Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps connectors. Administrators can manage the policies directly in Purview starting mid-March 2027.

keyChanges.title: Agent Builder guidance says Information Barriers hide restricted users
keyChanges.detail: The Information Barriers guidance adds that Agent Builder honors Information Barriers policies in its people picker, hiding users whom a person is restricted from communicating or collaborating with.

keyChanges.title: SAP S/4HANA scan guidance sets a 128 GB RAM recommendation
keyChanges.detail: The source-registration guidance now identifies SAP S/4HANA, rather than SAP ECC, as the memory-intensive scan requiring a recommended Self-hosted Integration Runtime machine with at least 128 GB of RAM.

2026-11-02.headline: Copilot DLP will exclude external email from grounding as retention coverage splits in 2027
2026-11-02.overview: Purview’s most consequential update is an admin-configurable DLP control that excludes email from external or untrusted domains from Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat grounding while preserving internal data use. The Message Center notice lists public preview in June 2026 and general availability in June 2027. Retention guidance separately sets January 15, 2027, as the point when “Teams chats and Copilot interactions” covers Teams content only; the remaining updates are mainly operational guidance for auto-labeling, simulations, and audit review.
2026-11-02.adminImpact: If Copilot retention coverage is required from January 15, 2027, create a separate retention policy using the “Microsoft Copilot Experiences” location; Teams retention behavior is unchanged. Plan auto-labeling against the 500,000-file-per-tenant-per-day aggregate ceiling across all policies, rather than treating it as a guaranteed rate. Use the added simulation statuses and audit activity names when interpreting results and records.

keyChanges.title: DLP adds external-email controls for Copilot grounding
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Purview is expanding DLP with an admin-configurable control for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat. It restricts processing of emails from external or untrusted domains, excluding them from Copilot grounding while internal data use continues. The Message Center notice lists public preview in June 2026 and general availability in June 2027.

keyChanges.title: Teams retention location drops Copilot interactions in 2027
keyChanges.detail: Beginning January 15, 2027, policies using “Teams chats and Copilot interactions” will apply only to Teams content and will no longer retain or delete Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions, including previously retained interactions. The guidance directs administrators to use a separate “Microsoft Copilot Experiences” location when Copilot retention is required.

keyChanges.title: The 500,000-file auto-labeling ceiling applies across all policies
keyChanges.detail: Information Protection guidance now defines 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant per day, aggregated across all auto-labeling policies, as an absolute ceiling. It is not a guaranteed processing rate, and actual throughput may be lower.

keyChanges.title: Simulation results distinguish failed jobs from requests that never started
keyChanges.detail: The Auto Label Simulation Results guidance adds the “Simulation failed” status, distinguishes failed jobs from requests that could not start, explains partial workload counts, and provides review and restart guidance. Administrators can preserve useful results before restarting and inspect workload details before enabling a policy.

keyChanges.title: Audit references add Power BI MCP semantic-model activities
keyChanges.detail: The Audit Log Activities reference now lists events for Power BI MCP tools that modify semantic models and read semantic-model metadata. Administrators can use these activity names when reviewing or interpreting audit records.

2026-11-09.headline: Purview will retire four DSPM partner integrations on December 7
2026-11-09.overview: The week’s clearest service-impacting change is the December 7, 2026 retirement of four DSPM partner integrations for non-Microsoft data sources. A broad Data Governance documentation sweep now adds notices saying Unified Catalog and classic Purview governance capabilities are being retired and consolidated in Microsoft Fabric and that new accounts can no longer be created. Other Message Center notices schedule adaptive-scope lifecycle controls, sensitivity labels for Microsoft Entra cloud security groups, and improved DLP setup for unmanaged apps in Edge for Business; Endpoint DLP’s Policy Sync and Device Health AI skills are slated for mid-2027 and require Security Copilot. Smaller updates clarify Insider Risk processing delays, the DLP location name “Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork,” and failed sensitivity-label audit operation names.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: Review dependencies on Varonis, BigID, Cyera, or OneTrust integrations before December 7; if none are used, the DSPM notice requires no action. For new governance work, do not plan on creating new Unified Catalog or classic Purview accounts, and factor the stated Fabric consolidation into roadmap decisions; the supplied documentation gives no migration deadline or procedure. For the announced future controls, verify licensing and separate enablement for Entra group labels. Update DLP configuration references to “Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork” and audit runbooks to use FileSensitivityLabelApplyFailed, FileSensitivityLabelChangeFailed, and FileSensitivityLabelRemoveFailed. Allow for Insider Risk scoring and alerts to continue during processing after group removal.

keyChanges.title: Four DSPM partner integrations have a December 7 retirement date
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft will retire the Varonis, BigID, Cyera, and OneTrust integrations for non-Microsoft data sources on December 7, 2026. They will stop ingesting and displaying data; other DSPM capabilities are unaffected. No action is required, but administrators using them should review dependencies.

keyChanges.title: Unified Catalog pages now say new Purview accounts cannot be created
keyChanges.detail: The updated Unified Catalog guidance says Unified Catalog and classic Microsoft Purview data governance capabilities, formerly Azure Purview, are being consolidated in Microsoft Fabric and that new accounts can no longer be created. It gives no deadline or specific migration step.

keyChanges.title: Adaptive scopes will default to active recipients and site owners
keyChanges.detail: Starting in December 2026 preview, adaptive scopes will evaluate only active recipients and site owners by default, with options to include inactive or soft-deleted ones; queries will support ISO 8601 durations. General availability is scheduled for April 2027, and no immediate action is required.

keyChanges.title: Sensitivity labels are coming to Microsoft Entra cloud security groups
keyChanges.detail: Starting mid-January 2027, Purview will support applying sensitivity labels to Microsoft Entra cloud security groups for label-based governance and access policies. The feature must be enabled separately and requires appropriate licensing; labels cannot yet be changed or removed once applied.

keyChanges.title: Edge unmanaged-app DLP adds Intune multi-admin approval support
keyChanges.detail: Starting late November 2026, Purview DLP will improve setup and activation for unmanaged apps in Edge for Business, add Intune multi-admin approval, and provide clearer status, detailed errors, and coordination between Purview and Intune administrators. No policy migration is needed.

2026-11-16.headline: Purview expands DLP to local AI agents, Azure Firewall traffic, and non-Microsoft apps
2026-11-16.overview: The week is led by three staged DLP expansions: protection for supported local AI-agent prompts, responses, and tool interactions; an Azure Firewall integration covering network text, files, and AI interactions; and connector-based DLP and auto-labeling for Google Workspace, Box, and Salesforce. Updated eDiscovery guidance also makes Teams purge permanence and sequencing explicit, while Data Lifecycle Management is set to apply 120-day retention labels to content deleted by elevated-risk users through Adaptive protection.
2026-11-16.adminImpact: Most feature notices point to 2027 preview or general-availability milestones. Local AI-agent DLP requires no enablement action, while Azure Firewall activation is described as automatic. For eDiscovery operations, use separate mailbox and Teams purge requests, purge Teams first, and treat teamsMessages purges as irreversible; the API returns 202 Accepted with a status URL. Administrators evaluating Adaptive protection should account for its 120-day retention-label behavior.

keyChanges.title: Local AI-agent interactions enter the DLP rollout plan
keyChanges.detail: Purview Data Loss Prevention is scheduled to cover supported local AI-agent prompts, responses, and tool interactions. Public preview is planned for late January 2027 and general availability for late April 2027; the notice says no action is required to enable it.

keyChanges.title: Azure Firewall adds network-data DLP coverage
keyChanges.detail: The DLP and Azure Firewall integration is scheduled to roll out in preview from mid-November 2026, with general availability in late April 2027. It covers sensitive network traffic, including text, files, and AI interactions, and supports automatic tenant activation and policy configuration without disrupting existing policies.

keyChanges.title: Connectors extend DLP and auto-labeling to non-Microsoft apps
keyChanges.detail: Purview will support DLP and auto-labeling for applications including Google Workspace, Box, and Salesforce through Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps connectors. Administrators will be able to manage the policies directly in Purview starting in mid-March 2027.

keyChanges.title: eDiscovery guidance specifies irreversible Teams purge sequencing
keyChanges.detail: Updated Microsoft Graph guidance says a teamsMessages purge permanently deletes Teams messages regardless of purgeType. Mailbox and Teams purges require separate requests, with Teams purged first; the API returns 202 Accepted with a status URL.

keyChanges.title: Adaptive protection adds 120-day retention for elevated-risk deletions
keyChanges.detail: The announced Data Lifecycle Management integration with Adaptive protection auto-applies retention labels to content deleted by elevated-risk users for 120 days, with minimal administrator setup. The notice describes a public preview and targets general availability in early 2027.

2026-11.headline: Purview governance shifts toward Fabric as DLP expands across Copilot and networks
2026-11.overview: November’s substantive changes combine a governance transition with a broader DLP perimeter. Updated Unified Catalog and classic Purview data-governance guidance now says those capabilities are being retired and consolidated in Microsoft Fabric, and that new accounts can no longer be created. Separately, Microsoft scheduled the retirement of four DSPM partner integrations for December 7, 2026. Message Center notices also stage DLP controls for excluding external email from Copilot grounding, protecting network traffic through Azure Firewall, and covering non-Microsoft applications through Defender for Cloud Apps connectors.
2026-11.adminImpact: Do not plan new Unified Catalog or classic Purview governance accounts; the supplied guidance gives no migration deadline or procedure, so Fabric consolidation is roadmap context rather than a documented migration runbook. If Varonis, BigID, Cyera, or OneTrust integrations are used for non-Microsoft data sources, review those dependencies before December 7 because they will stop ingesting and displaying data; other DSPM capabilities remain unaffected. For the announced DLP expansions, track the stated preview and general-availability milestones, noting that the Copilot control is admin-configurable, Azure Firewall activation is described as automatic, and non-Microsoft app coverage depends on Defender for Cloud Apps connectors.

keyChanges.title: Unified Catalog guidance now says new account creation is unavailable
keyChanges.detail: Updated guidance for Unified Catalog and classic Purview data-governance capabilities says they are being retired and consolidated in Microsoft Fabric, and that new accounts can no longer be created. The supplied update provides no migration deadline or procedure.

keyChanges.title: Four DSPM partner integrations are scheduled for December 7 retirement
keyChanges.detail: The Varonis, BigID, Cyera, and OneTrust integrations for non-Microsoft data sources will no longer ingest or display data after December 7, 2026. Other DSPM capabilities remain unaffected; administrators using these integrations should review their dependencies.

keyChanges.title: Copilot DLP will exclude external email from grounding
keyChanges.detail: The new admin-configurable control restricts Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat from processing email from external or untrusted domains. Those messages are excluded from Copilot grounding while internal data remains available; the notice lists public preview in June 2026 and general availability in June 2027.

keyChanges.title: Azure Firewall integration extends DLP to network traffic
keyChanges.detail: The integration covers sensitive network text, files, and AI interactions. Rollout begins with preview in mid-November 2026 and reaches general availability by late April 2027, with automatic tenant activation, policy configuration, and no disruption to existing policies described.

keyChanges.title: DLP and auto-labeling are coming to connected non-Microsoft apps
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Purview will support DLP and auto-labeling for applications such as Google Workspace, Box, and Salesforce through Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps connectors. Administrators will be able to manage the policies directly in Purview starting in mid-March 2027.
